One of the men who signed the Dedham Covenant in 1637, founding the town of Dedham,
Massachusetts. He moved on to Medfield and then to the Connecticut River frontier.
On 18 September 1675, in King Philip's War, he was killed at Bloody Brook, near Deerfield,
when warriors ambushed a company of soldiers and teamsters carting the Deerfield harvest;
three of his sons died with him. His son Ephraim's daughter Experience brought the name Hinsdale into the line:
her son was Hinsdale Clark. Ann, wife of Robert Hinsdale of Dedham and Medfield;
she died about 1668, seven years before her husband was killed at Bloody Brook.
